data: Amazing game with a very good story
+ Great gameplay, very fun to play
great game with many hours of fun
it is a really good game the graphics are awesome its just great
Definitely worth it, and definitely worth the price
Don't get me wrong the game isn't unplayable it's just very unpolished and shallow
, the story is just so boring and repetitive
it feels so hollow and empty and the gameplay is really unfun
sadly it very quickly becomes a boring and lifeless grind
I can't recommend anyone to spend money on this
Thought I finally found a casual game that doesn't make you go in caves and do fighting. Nope, you have to do fighting zZz!!! Ruined it for me.

I appreciate the artistry and the music of the game. I absolutely love the “speaking” part of the game. For those of us that are aged and having weakening eyes, it is fantastic when we can “Hear” the conversations instead of trying to read through it all. A Great BIG THANK YOU for that. The quests are really well integrated. The only part at the moment I am having issues with is the abandoned ruin. It is most likely my eyesight, but it is not well lit and most of cave/area gray even with the miner’s helm. Other than that, this game is very nice. I do see my self getting the other “My Time at” games very soon.

Game is really fun and I was really absorbed into it.
Overall a game that is worthy of its selling price as its quite a big world and lots of quest .
There are also mods that others have made to make the game more fun or easier if you think its difficult.

Problems -
Some bugs and errors , such as crashing or fatal error when doing certain stuff.
Not everyone has the same bugs. Unable to save the game until the end of the game day. Kind of a bummer when you crash and you gotta redo the whole day

This is game has been a lot of fun to watch develop and progress into its current form. It isn't as in-depth as Stardew or as all-around amazing as Rune Factory, but it is great fun and gives you a lot of things to do and explore. I recommend trying it out if you are looking for a relaxing crafting sim.

I actually enjoy this game more than I do stardew valley. I bought it back in 2019 right before the pandemic hit and I'm glad I did because this kept me entertained for hours while I was stuck at home. This game is a masterpiece and Sand rock is just as fun!

This is a well made game that allows hours of fun. It has meaningful character relationships that'll make you both happy, sad, and angry. The farming aspect of this game actually is not that important - you can get through the main quest without ever planting or raising any animals. However, the building aspect is unique and fun.

Good game, but a bit too long and tedious, especially when you need some rare materials which either require a lot of grinding ( Tempering liquid, carbon fibers, etc. ) or trees/plants that take a lot of time to grow ( materials to make pigments and concrete for instance ).

It also feels unfinished with a lot of missing voice lines, lots of typos ( you might have guessed that from the title alone ), weird menus that meke no sense ( tree farm ), and a really bad combat system.

But if you like this kind of game there is a lot of content and you can keep playing after the "end", building your relationships with npcs, getting a spouse, upgrading your estate, decorating your house, etc.

The factory is a cool idea which makes tha crafting a lot easier and faster, so get it as fast as you can. And get the irigation floor from the church and start growing all the trees early, believe me you're going to need them...

The concept is nice but the game feels unpolished and more like an early access
The biggest issue is the movement and combat. My expectations weren't high since this is a life sim but the controls really feels terrible, the combat is also very basic.
I like the game's visual style, it's what got me to buy the game in the first place but the characters look kinda bad. The faces are pretty uncanny, characters with very cartoonishly shaped heads and tiny eyes just don't work. Along with the voice acting/dialogue sounding unnatural with the occasional audio errors.

My most favorite non-sci-fi single player game! It has combat, survival and social aspects. I admit it could have wider social interactions but the devs still made an amazing job and I enjoyed every minute of playing Portia :)
This game is SO ADDICTING I spend HOURS on it. It's like minecraft+thesims it's so much fun PLS PLAY I need more people knowing this game
Portia is a beautiful place and very relaxing with fun and interesting characters. I love the building aspect and is the perfect game to unwind to.

I really loved this. The gameplay loop is satisfying (even if it does get a bit grindy at times) and the characters are charming. I got a bit choked up when a bunch of NPCs turned up in front of my house on my in-game birthday to give me presents. Haha.

I also appreciated that there was a storyline to follow. While I love just faffing about, it's nice to have an overarching narrative to tie the game together.

this game is quite recommended based on graphic, story lines, and crafting
based on my perspective the minus in this game is, this game lack of tutorial for new player and farming quite useless in this game.
the corps sold in low price and you need some time to cook them.
I prefer fishing to get money.

I only played 2 hours so far and I'm already enjoying the game to the TOP. If this game was multiplayer it would have been huge, it's giving me that nostalgic vibes of some old mmorpgs I played in my childhood, for real I wish it was multiplayer but it's not and that's kinda sad

This game is charming, easy to play, and so far, utterly addicting. Just existing and reshaping this little 3d world is a treat in and of itself. That being said, for the love of god PLEASE add some kind of co op feature. The only thing more fun than this game itself would be being able to do so with a friend.
The most unstable crashing I have ever experienced in a game. Combine this with the fact that you cannot save the game at-will, and I have had more lost progress than saved progress 5 hours in.

I really like the whole concept of the game and how the story progresses. The thing I have an issue with is a reoccurring problem that happens when I have to tab out to change a song or show that i'm playing on my second monitor. When I tab out it cause the game to crash and if I don't save a whole days progress is lost, which is very annoying.

I thought it was a remake of an old builder game I have on steam I cannot locate. This game is the same as finding paradise. If you have time to manage a farm on a primitive level while gathering non-existent resources. This game is a total waste of time.

My time at portia is a game that shows alot of promise. I've got about 40 hours in and got the main storyline done so far.
If you enjoy a farming game this game is one you'll enjoy, it has alot of variation in content and has alot of charm on top of that.

The main gathering gameplay is fluid and smooth and the targeting feels responsive enough to make not feel like you have to struggle to harvest something. A small gripe with the harvesting system is that it sometimes can be a little to sensitive as far as targeting goes. But most of the time this has not been an issue.

The progression system is nicely fleshed out, altho it might have been me missing the prompt that you're locked once a point is put in you can't get anymore in that part of the tree.

The social aspect of this game is nice, but i have yet to explore that part fully, the bonuses being typed out for each level of friendship is however really appreciated making it a good indicator to know who to work on during that time. However a neutral item list for gifts would be a good implementation.

Overall as far as this early access title goes i can heavily reccomend it.
this game is amazing. when you think the story line is done, you realize there's several more hours of gameplay to go. would recommend to anyone who enjoys farming sims

i got this game while it was on sale for $6. and let me say, even if it wasn't on sale, its for sure worth the buy. there is so much packed into this game and I have only been playing for a good 5 hours. i became interested in this game as I heard people saying it's like a 3D Stardew Valley, and while I can say I do see that, I promise you there is a lot of features that sets this apart from Stardew. its so much fun and i love it so much.
i really enjoyed the story line and crafting. only thing the camera moment can make you felt sickness

Portia is a very chill game, perfect for those days in which you come back form work exhausted and don't want to go to bed yet, but at the same time you haven't the energy to jump in full action killing bosses or players.
The graphics are cute and the stories are actually really good!

This game is great - a lot of fun to play!!! If you like gathering, crafting, mining, relationship building, farming, etc. this is a must! To me it's a lot like Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley, and to some extent Rune Factory - which are all games I really enjoy. I'd love to be able to build a Golf cart/ATV/4-wheeler-type vehicle to cruise around in and I'd especially like to see more "attractive" male bachelors... Another thing I think would be awesome is the ability to add your own reminders/notes on the calendar as I'm always forgetting Saturday morning inspections... :) I would definitely give this game a 10/10 and I'm really excited to see where it goes from here.

LOVE THIS GAME. Feels like im playing Harvest Moon with combat rpg. Highly enjoyable and would recommend to anyone who likes harvest moon and stardew similar games.

My tips are
Never sell an item that u cant easily get.

Fishing is my main source to farm gold.

Make materials in advance that way it will be a lot easier to finish every commision u pick.

ALWAYS FARM WOODS.

build multiple furnace for fast making mats.

ALWAYS PICK HERBS & ANIMAL FECES FOR FERTILIZER AND HERBAL JUICE(POTION FOR DUNGEON)

I had heard from it from the Stardew Valley fandom and bought it recently because it was 75% on sale. Yes, it was hard at first to open the game but messing around with the setting helped. :)
Now, it runs pretty smothly on my parents computer if I don't have to much stuff open at the same time.

Scratches the Stardew Valley itch for task completion and collection and decorating but in a different way. Story was ok mining is annoying AF at first until you get better tools but I suppose thats the point. All in all worth getting on sale

I bought this game years ago on my xbox one and then I bought it here on sale. I honestly love this game. The progression is nicely paced. I love that certain missions help you learn more about characters or even give you more commissions when at the main building you can only accept one a day there. The story is interesting all the way through.

My only cons would be at times I could accept a commission that I didn't even have any access to where I could get the materials to make the items to complete. I had to look up the item and find out online that I couldn't even make it yet without major story progression. (This had, however happened when playing on xbox one and specifically when it was still in early access.)

One other con would be that some of the characters faces are a bit strange looking, but once you get past that, the characters themselves are pretty interesting and have some nice dialogue.
this game is fun and so many interaction. the grafic is great and the eviroment is beautiful

At first, I did not think this would be for me. The nature of this game is so opposite of my usual kinds of games. I'm a Minecrafter, a Raftonian, Ark, Fallout, the list goes on. It has been a few decades for me to do anything so single player Final Fantasy like. And it is not quite like FF but it is in many ways so abstracted from my usual fare.

However, I simply tried it without any preset goals in my mind. Just tried making some money, tried satisfying various contracts, actually just tried the game as if I was a young person without any preconcieved notions. And it worked, I fell in love with this game.

Added complication: I'm a brain injury survivor. Stroke level memory issues so I am constantly struggling to find this place or that place yet, I can promptly regain my bearings and be productive. It is easy for people to mistakenly think that I am mentally impaired. I am not, I suffered brain damage, yes, however the impairments that exist have little to do with intellect. This game is on some levels a touch frightening with all the possible avenues of gaming it presents. It is not out of reach even for me.

So, you should be able to readily and easily enjoy what successes you can accomplish.
Once you get those under your belt, you'll be eager to move forward on the more in depth detailed ones.

Where to begin? I have never ever played a game as diverse, fun, energetic and as full of non stop action as this game. Theres a phrase called K.I.S.S which stands for keep it simple stupid and this game is not only simple but very diverse and complex. The world is ever expanding, the things you craft are never dull and the missions and lore are incredibly fun. At the time of me writing this I have over 120 hours sunk into this game and I have not been bored for a single hour. Combat is good. Interacting with everyone else in the town makes it feel like you have a personal connection with everyone there. There are different events depending on what season it is for instance the winter season includes snowball fights and Halloween season has a haunted cave and ghost hunt. It's a phenomenal time that I have not regretted playing and neither will you

I've enjoyed it a lot, one caveat though - I've used mods for most of my play time.
But still it's a very good game mostly based around crafting and gathering.
City events and friendships with npcs were really good.
A lot of things to do. City changing as you do quests was a very nice touch.

But yeah QoL mods and crafting speed adjustment helped my enjoyment big time.

Good Crafting system, has a very Stardew feel with the villagers and their personalities, stories and requests. Farming while it is in the game is a minor portion of the gameplay. While it does have its lull periods, a day of crafting to catch up on materials needed pushes through it. You can speed through the story if you know what you're doing or enjoy the slower pace and lot of gameplay. Overall it's fun, engaging and worth picking up.

I really like to play My Time At Portia. It's a really relaxing game and there's always something to do. You can mine, craft stuff, build, play games, date, fish, explore, battle monsters.
My Time At Portia is familiar to games like Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley, Animal Crossing, Coral Island, Littlewood, Graveyard Keeper.
If you like this game, then definitely also check out My TIme at Sandrock!

Hello Developers. I hope you guys release new updates or patches to fix the game suddenly crashes. Encountered this for a couple of times already. I wasted lots of hours of progress just because the game crashed. Or at least please make some kind of like Quick Save option for us to save the game without going to sleep. Please fix this issue ASAP. Thank you.

This game is awesome, it is chill and relaxing and a whole lot of fun. Crafting system is not too basic but not crazy complex either. Interesting ways to collect needed materials. Farm crops, craft, gather wood/stone and more. Be the ultimate hoarder! Even for Early Access it feels very solid, no bugs encountered so far. Quests are fun too.

PLEASE ADD MULTIPLAYER!! Not even Co-op just let two people (or more) buy workshops on the island and build them so people can play with their RL spouse/family/friends at the same time.

Have not encountered anything to complain about yet. Very happy with purchase

The game is quite boring. The gameplay gets quite repetitive, and the horrible controls don't help either. All the characters remind me of the Metaverse, and their dialogue is so robotic.

All in all, a pretty poor farming game.
This was a game I should have loved, but in practice it was painfully tedious and soulless.

I dunno why it stopped going up at exactly 20 hours, but I have played quite a bit of this, probably somewhere more like 80-90 total. I like it. It's got a charm. I've been dabbling on and off wit hit for a long time now and it's come quite a long way. It's comfy. It's a tiny bit jank but you know what it be. Crafting, building(more like placing, to be frank and fair), bosses, relationships, it's neat. I'd recommend it for 25-30 buckaroons. 90% recommend in general, If you catch it on sale 100% reccommend

My Time at Portia is very chill and easy to accidentally play for 3+ consecutive hours. It does sometimes crash, which can be frustrating, but it also autosaves at the end/beginning of every day. It doesn't feel as grind-y as Harvest Moon often gets, and it's very low-stakes if you wanna focus on mining versus farming versus fighting. There are lots of fun (bisexual!) options for romantic partners, and my only complaint in that arena is the lack of nonbinary options (visually very gender, but the voices and some other minor things can be quite binary). I also like that there are plotlines that periodically and sporadically appear, so it isn't exclusively driven by the player's own desire to get better at things.

Update (27/9/23): I haven't picked it up much since I started playing it because there's so much to do and the map is so large and there are so many people that it's honestly a bit overwhelming for me to think about getting back into. Very good for people bored by the usual HM options who want Rune Factory But More, but if you're looking for a game you can have more of a completionist attitude toward, this might be a bit much. (also, the thing where it semi-regularly crashed did get very old, though that may have been more old laptop more than the game)

I finished the main story and the Majority of the Side missions as far as a story rich stand point it has a very good story. There is a lot of fluff in the game gets a little grindy at times. It has its bugs some story mission bugs i had to install a mod to fix. As far as game play goes it was fantastic controls were just a little clunky to get used to but all in all once you got the hang of them it was great. This is not a short game. Also I didnt care to much for the level wall. I believe that this game is a fun game that I really enjoyed despite some of its downfalls.
A cute relaxing game, it has a nice flow and it's easy to get into the zone with completing tasks and exploring the world.
Very good game 10/10 but they took away the button that teleports you out of the mines which kinda ruins the whole experience for me. Love the game though the crafting is top tier
Its so addictive time just disapears when you think you have played for an hour or two you look at the clock and a few hours have passed

The perfect game if you just want to kick back and get lost in a different world - one that offers continuous tasks that keep you engaged. The characters are interesting and varied, of a depth level I personally would even consider more than Stardew Valley. I highly enjoyed it!

I personally did not stumble upon many bugs, but some voice over tracks were missing. This seems to have been remedied over time, whoever. I have not verified this, though.

I played this game near release and loved it. I understood it was early access and even still the game was smooth and easily playable with great and addicting crafting progression. I came back to the game after a while and hoping to enjoy it just as much, if not more since they added new content, and I was sorely disappointed. Almost immediately I was slapped in the face with fps drops. After upgrading my computer since the last time the game was played I actually had to reduce the graphics to play without skips, and then whenever something new happened in the game it would freeze for literal seconds.

For the most part after the initial spikes the game runs relatively okay. That is until the hazardous ruins. With a few unfortunate fps drops here and there I made it to the final boss. Not even half way into the bosses HP the game freezes solid which led to an ALT F4, losing all progression that day. I do enjoy this game a lot, it scratches that itch incredibly well for a progressive simulator. However I cannot recommend this game in the current state. Funny enough if you asked me a year ago and I wouldn't of hesitated.

When I bought this game I had some expectations that it would be a pleasant game to play, but in fact there are at least two things in the game that made me change my mind, the first one is to be grinding and progress in the main story is too slow for my taste.

Despite these two factors I cannot give this game a bad review, because the game itself is quite consistent in lot of things such as, in level of the crafting system, where there are several items to build and discover, the social level, where all inhabitants each one of them has its own history and personality, the battles against enemies, the game presents a varied list of gear to use, in terms of exploration, each location has its own items to collect and enemy to defeat and events that occur during the year, where by participating in them there is an associated token where you can buy items.

And I think with the list mentioned above the game is quite appealing and balanced, which positively balances the game, in my opinion.

However, as I mentioned right at the beginning, the progress of this game is TOOOO slow, but feel free to try this game if you want it.

It's no where near done yet. I just was farming for items in the ruin, of course with sand and dirt and rock bag gets full. Go to delete item to pick up relic and it's gone. They've had issues paying their voice actors despite some pretty good income from sales/Kickstarter, so their characters are only half voiced. Items keep disappearing in sort all feature. And if you make a ton of items at once some will disappear a long with the resources used. I failed an a level quest because some of my steel magically vanished and now I can't select a new one. It's not ready don't spend your money. It has great potential but at this point bugs like these shouldn't be happening.

I love that the world of Portia isn't completely explained to players. There's a lot of mystery surrounded the events that set up the game, and you need to dig to find answers. I'm on my second playthrough and I feel like there are some mysteries the narrative never solves. You're left to wonder what caused the end of the world and how the survivors rebuilt it.

Also there are fun NPCs, creatively designed monsters, simple combat mechanics, and gorgeous graphics.

tldr.text: Very Positive (92%) on Steam, and players love the story and characters.
The main complaint is bugs and crashes.

details.text: Recent reviews are as positive as the all-time score, at 92%, so the mood has stayed steady.
New players are much less positive than veterans: 47% of those with under two hours liked it, against 96% of those with over fifty hours.
